title: Dutch roadside-grass availability and mowing evidence from national and regional sources
source_location: Rijkswaterstaat: official Bermonderhoud page, introduction and section ‘Maaien en snoeien’; Zuid-Holland: Sections ‘We gaan (minder) maaien’, ‘Elke weg een eigen maaiplan’, and ‘Bermzeep’; Utrecht Region: ARBOR Chapter 3, §§3.2.1–3.2.3, pp. 10–11
authors: Rijkswaterstaat; Provincie Zuid-Holland; interview with provincial green-asset staff; ARBOR report editors Gohar Nuhoff-Isakhanyan and Emiel Wubben and case-study contributors
persistent_identifier: 0f08e50f-6483-4d62-8a29-16a049e5c5ec (persistent government dataset identifier; not a DOI); ARBOR report has no DOI
license: Rijkswaterstaat management page and provincial article: no dataset-specific reuse license stated; provincial open-data catalog: public domain; ARBOR report: no explicit reuse license identified.
geography: Multiple Netherlands comparators: Rijkswaterstaat motorway network; Province of Zuid-Holland; Utrecht Region (Province of Utrecht plus Het Gooi in North Holland)
evidence_class: official operational reporting; aggregate quantity and schedule

reported_values.annual_mown_verge_grass: approximately 10,000 t/year; wet/dry mass basis, reference year, and metering method unstated
reported_values.provincial_inventory_estimates: 46,100 t in a previous inventory and 60,102 t in a later inventory; both reported in the provincial 2023 report; underlying reference years, mass bases, and detailed calculation inputs are unresolved
reported_values.annual_municipal_green_waste: 76,084 t/year across Zuid-Holland municipal green waste; mixed composition; dataset updated 2026-08-13; reference year and mass basis unstated
reported_values.annual_mowing_rounds: Zuid-Holland reports two rounds, June–July and September–October; Rijkswaterstaat says motorway grass is mown once yearly in most cases, with local variation
reported_values.collection_timing: Zuid-Holland page says mown material is left in the field for a few days before collection; exact duration unstated
reported_values.utrecht_region_annual_collected: approximately 60,000 tonnes/year mown, collected, and processed; mass basis, reference year, and measurement method unstated
reported_values.utrecht_region_annual_uncollected: approximately 70,000 tonnes/year remains after mowing and is not collected; report says leaving it depends on biodiversity and traffic-safety conditions
reported_values.utrecht_region_reported_total_potential: approximately 130,000 tonnes/year, the report's sum of its collected and uncollected categories; not all collected or accessible
reported_values.utrecht_region_mowing_schedule: typically two rounds per year, May–June and September–October, as described in the 2015 report
reported_values.rws_mowing_schedule: once per year in most cases; locations may be mown more frequently depending on vegetation and road-safety risk; exact routes and dates not given

applicability: Regional maintenance context only; the quantity is not the GreenHub contracted or delivered supply and is not connected to model defaults or scenario availability.
limitations: Undated page; reference year is not given.
Mass basis and measurement method are not stated; do not convert to dry matter.
No per-road or per-round tonnage, contamination fraction, access constraint, or GreenHub allocation is reported.

The 76,084 t/year municipal dataset includes verge grass, pruning residues and other public-space green waste; it cannot be used as roadside-grass supply without category-level records and basis clarification.
Mowing regimes differ between Rijkswaterstaat, provincial, municipal, and ecological management; reported national summaries are not route calendars.

The ARBOR Utrecht-region quantities are approximate project-reported estimates; their underlying reference year, wet/dry basis, measurement method, site records, and collection constraints are not supplied. The 130,000 t/year figure is the report's total of the preceding categories and must not be counted again as a separate stream.

The 46,100 t and 60,102 t inventory figures are distinct calculated estimates based on differing source material, not repeat weighbridge measurements; do not interpret their difference as a measured temporal increase or combine them with the approximately 10,000 t provincial-road figure, 117/120 t GreenHub reports, or mixed municipal green-waste totals.
